note: Taiwan: nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa for 90 days (Honduras included; British and Canadian stays extendable to 180, not modelled), 30 or 14 days (Oman, Thailand, Brunei and the Philippines, the last three until 31 July 2027); only British citizens' passports qualify, so the British territories' passports need a visa. Nationals of Bahrain, Bosnia, Dominica, Ecuador, Haiti, Kuwait, Mauritius, Montenegro, Oman (beyond 14 days), Panama, Peru, Qatar, Russia (to 6 July 2027), Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and the UAE may apply for an eVisa; Armenia, Colombia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan only with a Schengen or US visa or residence (taken as a visa). Hong Kong and Macao residents apply beforehand for an entry and exit permit (5 business days; 3 months' stay), and mainland Chinese under their own permit regime: both taken as a visa. Everyone else needs a visa from a mission. North Macedonia's exemption runs to 31 March 2030; place-of-birth exclusions and the Online Travel Authorization for some South-east Asian nationals holding a Western visa aren't modelled.

sources.title: Bureau of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Taiwan), Visa-Exempt Entry (updated 17 July 2026)
sources.said: Nationals of the following countries are eligible for the visa-exemption program, with a duration of stay of up to 90 days: Albania, Andorra, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Eswatini*, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan*, Kosovo, Republic of Korea, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Marshall Islands*, Monaco, Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia*(effective until March 31, 2030), Norway, Palau, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Tuvalu*, United Kingdom*, and United States of America*. Nationals of the following countries are eligible for the visa-exemption program, with a duration of stay of up to 30 days: Belize*, Malaysia, Saint Kitts and Nevis*, Saint Lucia*, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and Singapore. Nationals of Honduras*, except those holding diplomatic or official/service passports, are eligible for the visa-exemption program, with a duration of stay of up to 90 days. Nationals of Dominican Republic, except those holding diplomatic or official/service passports, are eligible for the visa-exemption program, with a duration of stay of up to 30 days. Nationals of Oman are eligible for the visa-exemption program, with a duration of stay of up to 14 days. Nationals of the Kingdom of Thailand (effective until July 31, 2027), ... Nationals of Brunei (effective until July 31, 2027), ... Nationals of the Philippines (effective until July 31, 2027), ... Only the United Kingdom passport holders with British Citizen status are eligible for visa-exempt entry.

sources.title: Bureau of Consular Affairs (Taiwan), General Information on eVisa Application
sources.said: Nationals of the following countries are eligible for an eVisa when they meet relevant criteria: Armenia*, Bahrain, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia*, Dominica, Ecuador, Haiti, Kazakhstan*, Kuwait, Mauritius, Montenegro, Oman, Panama, Peru, Qatar, Russia*, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye*, United Arab Emirates, Uzbekistan*. ... For the period March 31, 2026, through March 31, 2027, nationals of Armenia, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan must provide a valid visa or resident certificate issued by a Schengen country ... Russia: Only holders of ordinary passports are eligible for an eVisa, effective from July 7, 2026, to July 6, 2027.

sources.title: National Immigration Agency (Taiwan), 0401 Guidelines for Hong Kong and Macao Residents to Apply for Entry and Exit Permits over the Counter
sources.said: The processing time is five business days ... V. Duration of stay: The duration of stay starts from the day after entry and must not exceed three months.
